newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Royal Brunei considers separate cargo unit.
newsitem.headline: Royal Brunei considers separate cargo unit.

text.p: Royal Brunei Airlines is considering setting up a separate cargo division as part of an ambitious expansion programme to put a bigger emphasis on air cargo and become a global carrier by the year 2000, senior airline officials told Reuters.

The 100 per cent Government-owned "niche" airline of the tiny sultanate intends to strengthen its role as both a passenger and cargo hub at the heart of south east Asia and expand its international route network.
During a visit to Hong Kong to outline the airline's goals, senior executives said their long term aim was to emulate neighbouring Singapore and world leading Singapore Airlines.
As management consider widespread changes after a two year long company review, Brunei intends to be put on the map and overcome its image of being a backwater, they said.

"We are toying with the idea of making cargo a separate entity. The decision has not yet been made but it has been seriously voiced. We intend to focus much more on cargo," Peter Oei, Area Manager, Orient told Reuters.
"The global concept is not something we have dreamed up overnight. We have a clear strategic aim to expand the hub and spoke concept and we are saying we are getting in shape to expand," he added.
New services to Honolulu, Paris, Ho Chi Minh City and Muscat in Oman are scheduled for this year. Expansion of services into China are also planned including new tourist services to Hainan Island.

Until the airline started investing in larger Boeing 767 aircraft, Royal Brunei carried "very little" cargo, said Captain Mike Fox, the airline's director of flight operations. Royal Brunei used to have a Boeing 737 Combi but as passenger 737s were replaced by larger Boeing 757 aircraft the Combi also left the the fleet in 1988.

"The Combi was a bit of a problem for us because it only carried cargo into Brunei, it was very one directional. The same is still true to some extent but we have seen there was surplus capacity under the floor and the last three years we have seen the potential and we are looking at using Brunei as a cargo hub using our increasing connections. Already increasing amounts of freight from Manila and Australia goes onward to Europe," Fox said.
One big development is the first stepping stone to a trans-Pacific service with three times weekly flights to Honolulu aimed largely at tourists from around Asia using Brunei as a hub.
Royal Brunei has nine Boeing 767-300 ER, two Boeing 757 and two Fokker 100 jets. Both Boeing and Airbus salesmen are wooing the airline now considering long term purchases, the executives said.

"The fleet mix we have is pretty good for the next 3 or 4 years then we will probably have to change it and we are facing that decision now. The 777 may be a bit big for us but we will see," Fox added.
The Brunei government also has plans to create an 'airport city' and develop airport facilities to cope with the anticipated traffic influx. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
